title: Palm Springs
sub: Two clocks: what the film shows you, and what actually happens. The chop here is not shuffled scenes — it is one day, hit over and over.
notes: The repetition: positions 2-12 on the right spine are not distinct dates, they are one day (9 November) replayed. A strict 1..N spine cannot give two scenes the same position, so the repeated day is unfolded once — the wake, the passes at it, then its evening and night — and every loop scene points into that one column. So read each node's two numbers as 'where the film puts it' and 'where in the day it lives'; where the ribbons run back up the spine, that cut is the loop resetting.

Only four things happen once in real time: the 8th of November (Sarah and Abe, position 1, screened eighth as the film's late reveal), the pass Sarah follows Nyles into the cave on, the pass she blows the cave up on, and the 10th (position 13). Everything between is one day repeating.

The film opens with Nyles already inside the loop: his own first pass at 9 November, and the long stretch of passes before Sarah arrives, are never screened — which is why the opening scene already sits deep in the column rather than at its start.

The last stretch runs straight: the final wedding, the cave, and the morning after are the only part of the film told end to end. Roy's reconciliation with Nyles in Irvine is folded into his hunting beat; the mid-credits scene is placed last although its date is deliberately unresolved (Roy is still looping, Nyles is not).
legend_note: Node numbering: left spine = screening position, right spine = position in the day. Where a ribbon runs back up the spine, the film has cut back to the start of the same day.
